findings.effect: The per-word search has no word limit, and each word adds 8 regex clauses. Neither the query schema nor the agent tool caps the search length or word count, so long queries get much slower as query length grows.
findings.reason: Both search schemas accept unbounded strings, and the new implementation generates eight regex predicates per word for both database queries, allowing excessive query construction and execution work.

findings.effect: The invitation seed checks only for an existing pending invitation, so it can create another pending invitation after the original is accepted or declined. After acceptance, this leaves a journey participant holding a pending invitation to the same journey, a state the service forbids.
findings.reason: Rerunning the seed after acceptance creates another pending invitation because it checks only pending invitations and bypasses the service’s existing-participant validation.
